result.answer:
Verdict: SUPPORTED

The paper reports 2,866 CSAT calls for training versus 362 for validation and 1,103 for testing, so validation plus test totals 1,465 calls—less than the 2,866 training calls [S:4a7219dd67e7#4]. CSAT is one of three evaluation datasets in the paper, alongside 20 newsgroups and Fisher Phase 1 [S:4a7219dd67e7#3].

claims.text: The CSAT dataset contains 4,331 calls split into 2,866 training, 362 validation, and 1,103 test calls.
claims.note: Span explicitly states 4331 calls split into 2866 training, 362 validation, 1103 testing.

claims.text: The CSAT validation and test splits total 1,465 calls (362 + 1,103), which is less than the 2,866 training calls.
claims.note: 362+1103=1465, and 1465 < 2866; both figures come from the same span, so the comparison is fully entailed.

claims.text: The paper evaluated its models on three datasets: CSAT, 20 newsgroups, and Fisher Phase 1.
claims.note: Span states models were evaluated on 3 datasets: CSAT, 20 newsgroups, Fisher Phase 1 corpus.

claims.text: The CSAT dataset consists of spoken transcripts produced automatically via ASR.
claims.note: Span describes CSAT as consisting of spoken transcripts (automatic via ASR).

citations.title: Hierarchical Transformers for Long Document Classification
citations.text:
CSAT dataset consists of US English telephone speech from call centers. For each call in this dataset,
customers participated in that call gave a rating on his experience with agent. Originally, this dataset
has labels rated on a scale 1-9 with 9 being extremely satisfied and 1 being extremely dissatisfied. Fig.
FIGREF16 shows the histogram of ratings for our dataset. As the distribution is skewed towards
extremes, we choose to do binary classification with ratings above 4.5 as satisfied and below 4.5 as
dissatisfied. Quantization of ratings also helped us to create a balanced dataset. This dataset contains
4331 calls and we split them into 3 sets for our experiments: 2866 calls for training, 362 calls for
validation and, finally, 1103 calls for testing.

citations.title: Hierarchical Transformers for Long Document Classification
citations.text:
Research extract  /  QASPER dev  /  arXiv 1910.10781
Hierarchical Transformers for Long Document Classification
Selected passages
ToBERT's computational complexity $O(\frac{n^2}{k^2})$ is asymptotically inferior to RoBERT, as the
top-level Transformer model again suffers from quadratic complexity in the number of segments.
However, in practice this number is much smaller than the input sequence length (${\frac{n}{k}} << n$),
so we haven't observed performance or memory issues with our datasets.
We evaluated our models on 3 different datasets:
CSAT dataset for CSAT prediction, consisting of spoken transcripts (automatic via ASR).
20 newsgroups for topic identification task, consisting of written text;
Fisher Phase 1 corpus for topic identification task, consisting of spoken transcripts (manual);
